title: Add staged prefetch tracer and shared KV cache sampling hook
author: Anya Patel
release_notes: Added staged prefetch tracer and a configurable shared KV cache sampling hook for low-overhead production sampling; features are opt-in via runtime flags.
description:
Context and motivation: Production latency spikes during long-tail generation workloads revealed two correlated contributors: (1) poorly observable prefetch scheduling behavior when multiple inflight requests cause competing KV cache prefetches, and (2) the overhead of dense NVTX instrumentation in high-throughput paths. This PR implements a lightweight, ticker-driven staged prefetch tracer and a shared KV cache sampling hook to make sampling cheaper and signal-rich for dashboarding and microbench collection. The feature is designed to be opt-in and safe for production rollout.

Goals: make it easy to: (a) sample prefetch decisions and cache evictions at low overhead, (b) correlate prefetch stages with kernel launch latency and queue depth without adding high-frequency NVTX ranges, and (c) export aggregated counters to existing perf dashboards and bench-lab harnesses for comparison across commits.

What changed (high-level): runtime/prefetch/staged_tracer.{cc,h} implements a ticker-based tracer that emits sparse NVTX ranges at stage boundaries and writes compact events into the ring buffer aggregator; runtime/kv/shared_sampler.{h,cc} adds a shared sampling hook with reservoir sampling and small histogram sketches; tools/benchlab/integrations/prefetch_microbench.py provides a microbench harness to replay scenarios; observability/exporters/perf_dashboard_adapter.go translates sketches into Prometheus-compatible histograms; configs/runtime_flags.yaml exposes feature flags.

Design notes and tradeoffs: sparse NVTX reduces instrumentation overhead by emitting ranges only on major stage transitions. The tracer uses a configurable tick (default 1ms) to batch events into the ring buffer and reduce contention. The shared sampler keeps a fixed-size reservoir per worker and merges reservoirs infrequently to bound memory and maintain sample quality. All features are gated behind runtime flags to retain backwards compatibility.

Benchmarks: benchlab scenarios (small-eval, long-gen, mixed-burst) on AWS p4d show a 3-7% p99 latency improvement for mixed-burst when replacing dense NVTX with staged tracer + sampler, and instrumentation CPU overhead dropped from ~2.1% to ~0.36% at default settings. Heavy-hitter sample coverage remained >90% at 1% sampling due to reservoir merge heuristics.

Testing and CI: unit tests cover reservoir merge and histogram sketch correctness; integration tests exercise benchlab replay against golden fixtures. Initial CI run hit a benchlab-smoke timeout due to an aggressive tick in CI containers; this was fixed by making the tick adaptive in container envs. Final CI status: all checks green.

Review highlights: Diego requested a tunable reservoir size; the author added runtime flag kvcache.reservoir_size with default 64. Mira asked about interaction with continuous batching; the tracer emits batch-level markers and per-sample IDs so dashboards can reconstruct lineage. Kofi approved after minor locking nits were addressed.

Follow-ups: wire sampler output into perf dashboard panels and add a prefetch heatmap; surface prefetch pressure to the dedicated scheduler; investigate adaptive sampling driven by observed variance.

Merge outcome: squashed and merged into main on 2026-02-25 after approvals and green CI. Bench artifacts stored under benchlab run id benchlab/2026-02-25/153567.
